# s250 — slicer merge-index must union note records appended on both sides

Two branches each appended a note to the same item, and the merge failed in two ways:

- `slicer merge-index` reported `conflict at items/db-11/note_records` and `items/db-16/note_records`, then exited 1, leaving `.slicer/index.json` unmerged. This happened when landing DataBall db-23 after db-18 (2026-10-11).
- Separately, the project's `.slicer/.gitattributes` assigned no merge driver to `index.json` at all, so git did a plain text merge. That repo has now been fixed; check whether `slicer init` and `setup-git` add the line.

Notes are append-only records with unique ids, so a three-way merge can always combine them safely.

**Findings:** DataBall db-23 landing, owner 2026-10-11 · **Size:** S · **Trees:** src/slicer, tests

**2026-10-11** — Ready for review: merge-index merges an item's note_records as the union by note id across base/ours/theirs, ordered by (created_at, id); a note removed on one side stays removed only if the other side left it unchanged; a note changed two ways conflicts at items/ID/note_records; non-plain note lists stay atomic. The index.json attribute was already written by init (ops.py GITATTRIBUTES), so test 5 is a regression guard. The old BothAppendToOneNoteList_Conflicts test was renamed KeepsBoth, and an extra deletion test was added. Gate VERDICT: PASS. Nits left: a non-string created_at raises TypeError in the sort (invalid state, already refused by model.py); same-second notes can be reordered by id; docs/getting-started.md:701 omits the delete-vs-edit conflict case.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** merging conflicting edits to non-note fields (status, fields, sections), which stay real conflicts.

## Why

Parallel slice relays now land one after another. Each relay files notes on shared later items such as db-11 and db-16, so this conflict will recur on every second landing. In the DataBall case the owner authorized a one-off manual resolution: union the note records by id, order them by `created_at`, then rerun the driver.

## Files

- `src/slicer` (`merge-index`): for each item, merge `note_records` as the union of base, ours and theirs, keyed by note `id`. Keep a deletion only if one side removed a note that existed in base and the other side left it unchanged. Order by (`created_at`, `id`). Other fields keep today's three-way rules.
- `src/slicer` (`init`/`setup-git`): make sure the project `.slicer/.gitattributes` maps `index.json merge=slicer-index`, the way it already maps `log.jsonl` and the renders.
- `tests`:
  - both sides append different notes to the same item, and the merge succeeds with both;
  - both sides append to different items;
  - the same note id appears on both sides with identical content, and it is kept once;
  - a real field conflict alongside note appends still fails, naming only the field;
  - `setup-git` output includes the `index.json` attribute.
